note: The ZMTP v1 handshake selects the vulnerable decoder and seeds it with the configured input batch size from attacker-controlled network traffic.
The stream engine asks the decoder for a receive buffer before reading bytes from the socket.
The decoder can expose its internal message buffer directly when the pending payload is at least as large as the allocator buffer.
After each socket read, the engine forwards the exact number of bytes read into resize_buffer, even though the v1 static allocator is fixed-size and does not need resizing.
The static allocator mutates only its recorded size, not the backing allocation, so later buffer decisions are based on attacker-influenced read lengths rather than the real fixed capacity.
Because the recorded allocator size can be reduced to the last read length, the zero-copy branch can be taken for a payload that still exceeds the actual static buffer capacity.
The decoder then schedules the message body to be written into the message storage chosen from the stale allocator state.
Network data is copied into the buffer pointer returned by the decoder, so an oversized zero-copy decision can direct the write past the fixed static allocation and crash the target.
